answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks through geospatial ground-truthing. Each agent verifies its physical presence by scanning an assigned knoll, measuring optical scatter off a reference marble marker, and sampling local yarrow spectra. An attacker incurs the verifiable capital cost of deploying discrete robotic platforms across distinct coordinates. However, atmospheric occlusion and seasonal vegetative decay perturb optical readings, falsely rejecting legitimate agents.
